messages:
oliver: heads-up, saw a 3x increase in host CPU for small chat requests after yesterday's kernel-picker roll. 95p latency for short streams jumped ~60ms.

maria: ugh. any flamegraphs or pprof?

oliver: yes, attached quick paste from pprof sampling: main threads spending ~70% of cycles in "tokenizer::decode_chunk" + syscall overhead on writev. kvcache hit-rate is fine. looks host-side parse + tiny writes to grpc are the culprit.

david: can you paste the pprof snippet? small writes == http2/GRPC hpack churn often.

oliver: pasted:
```
(pprof) top 10
20.3%  tokenizer::decode_chunk
18.7%  socket_writev
12.1%  parse::request_frame
8.9%   http2::hpack_encode
6.5%   kvcache::lookup
...
```

maria: interesting that kernel-picker change affected this. kernel selection shouldn't change preparse path. did the rollout change batching heuristics too?

kai: kernel change also swapped in the new mini-batch scheduler for some tenants. it has slightly different max_batch_delay (5ms -> 10ms) and a new prefork for preparse work. could be side-effect.

david: longer max_batch_delay could reduce CPU by increasing batching, but prefork threads doing preparse might be contending on the tokenizer pool.

oliver: agree. I instrumented thread states: preparse threads stuck in short syscalls (recvmsg/writev) and then calling into tokenize. We see a lot of 1-2 token requests causing writev of tiny frames (~120 bytes).

maria: two levers to try: coalesce small grpc writes on host proxy (writev buffer) and prefer minidecode path for <=16 token requests.

david: also bump: enable writev coalescing flag we had disabled for the kernel canary? that's config flag coalesce_small_writes=true on the proxy.

kai: flag is off for the new scheduler because it interacted poorly with the socket batching experiment. but we can A/B enable on 10% to measure.

oliver: quick local microbench: enabling coalesce_small_writes drops syscall rate ~40% and reduces tokenizer CPU by ~25% on emulated workload of many 1-4 token messages.

maria: nice. what about KV cache behavior? any additional latency from coalescing?

oliver: kvcache lookups unaffected; most time is preparse + syscalls. KV contribution was minor in pprof. However, we noticed KV coldstart spikes for a small shard recently — separate signal.

david: plan: 1) enable coalesce_small_writes on 10% with monitoring 2) short-circuit tokenizer to minidecode for tiny payloads 3) reduce prefork concurrency for preparse to avoid pool contention.

kai: I'll schedule the flag canary now. deploy-bot will report.

deploy-bot: rollout started: coalesce_small_writes=true on 10% of runtime hosts (group: canary-io).

oliver: I'll push a small patch to parse path that routes <=16 token inputs through minidecode path and adds a metric preparse.tokenizer_path.

maria: add a histogram for write size and syscall counts per request too. want to be able to see small-write distribution.

david: we should also check kernel selection fallback: if we pick a kernel variant that assumes larger IO shapes, it may disable coalesce heuristics. audit the kernel-picker config for coalesce flags.

kai: noted. I'll add a quick audit: grep for "coalesce" across kernel manifests.

oliver: post-mortem followups: collect pprof after canary and compare host CPU, syscall rate, 95p tail for short streams. leaving a TODO in the tracking ticket.

maria: cool. if canary improves, roll to 50% then stable. if not, revert and investigate further (maybe kernel change touched stream framing behavior).

david: one last note — also watch GCMALLOC logs; we saw small spikes in allocs during tokenizer path when switching to minidecode vs full tokenizer. might need a pooled buffer.

oliver: copy. adding buffer pool metric now. will post results in ~30m. :eyes:
